ops.text: Our $Q_{\star}^{\prime}$ is about an order of magnitude larger than the $Q_{\star}^{\prime}=1.94\times 10^{6}$ obtained for the G dwarf KELT-29 once its transit times are corrected for the star's line-of-sight acceleration [⟦new.B10⟧]. Had TOI-2109 dissipated as efficiently, Equation 7 with $q=0.00331$ and $a/R_{\star}=2.268$ would predict $\dot{P}\approx-38.1$ ms/yr for TOI-2109 b, roughly eleven times the rate we measure.
